short_summary: Houthi strikes on Riyadh airport have caused heavy damage to a commercial aircraft, flight suspensions, and widespread aviation disruptions.

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.title: Houthis claim attack on Riyadh airport as airlines suspend flights to Saudi capital

paragraphs: A series of severe escalations in the region led to significant disruption on Thursday after Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi movement claimed responsibility for a ballistic missile strike targeting the international airport in Saudi Arabia's capital, Riyadh. Although the group provided no direct evidence for the claim and Saudi authorities did not immediately issue an official comment, multiple sources confirmed serious incidents at the aviation hub. Witnesses heard multiple explosions across Riyadh, including a very large blast directly at King Khalid international airport. One witness speaking to the Associated Press confirmed that emergency fire and ambulance crews were rapidly deployed to the area. A video verified by news agencies showed thick black columns of smoke and towering flames rising from the terminal. The same witness, choosing to remain anonymous, stated that outgoing flights were halted immediately and that passengers were instructed to evacuate the terminal buildings.

According to three individuals briefed on the situation, shrapnel resulting from an interception or an incoming projectile struck a parked commercial aircraft belonging to Saudia Airlines. The plane subsequently caught fire and sustained heavy structural damage while parked at a terminal on Thursday. Observers noted that while passengers were not believed to be on board the aircraft at the time of the incident, officials could not completely rule out potential injuries on the ground. In response to the rapidly worsening security situation, several major international carriers, including Lufthansa and Air India, officially suspended their scheduled routes to Riyadh. Data compiled by aviation analytics firm Cirium revealed that nearly half of all scheduled departures from the capital's airport were canceled by 1500 GMT on Thursday. Further disruptions were anticipated, with 31 additional cancellations projected for Friday across airports throughout the kingdom.

This latest attack follows statements from Saudi authorities confirming on Wednesday that three individuals had been killed earlier in the week during strikes targeting airports in Riyadh and the southwestern city of Abha. Furthermore, Saudi officials reported that debris from an intercepted missile had struck a kindergarten and a medical complex within Riyadh. The Houthis escalated their military campaign on Thursday in an explicit attempt to shut down the kingdom's airspace entirely, while also warning workers to stay away from energy plants because those facilities would be targeted next.

The heightened hostilities coincide with a renewed offensive in Yemen's civil war. The Houthis stated they are targeting Saudi Arabia in retaliation for its military backing of the UN-recognised Yemeni government, which is fighting to take back territory. Over the past month, the Houthi movement has made a lightning advance across Yemen's coastal plain, gaining ground in the south-west by Wednesday as the group approached the city of Taiz. Independent observers warned earlier this week that the group was dangerously on course to capture Taiz, with clear signs that forces linked to the Saudi-backed government were pulling back in order to secure the major southern port city of Aden. Meanwhile, Riyadh is due to host a major meeting of international energy policymakers, specifically the WPC Energy Congress, this week.
